laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They can include long prison sentences and heavy fines.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Always carry your passport and visa. Routine police checks in public and tourist spots are common. You could be fined or jailed if you don't show a valid travel document when asked. Check with local authorities before you export any items. Azerbaijan has some gambling restriction
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Dress standards can be conservative outside of Baku. Public displays of affection may not be welcome. Dress conservatively, particularly at mosques and religious shrines. Take care not to offend. If in doubt, seek local advice.
laws.heading: Dress and behaviour

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships were decriminalised in 2000, but are not widely accepted. Intolerance, discrimination and violence towards LGBTQIA+ people happens in Azerbaijan. Avoid public displays of affection.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: For specific information, contact the nearest embassy or consulate of Azerbaijan.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: You can drive in Azerbaijan with a current Australian driver's licence. Foreigners staying for more than one month may need to get a local driver's licence through Azerbaijan Service and Assessment Network (ASAN) Service Offices. You may also need an International Driving Permit (IDP) for travel and car insurance. Check with your insurer and car provider before you drive.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: The Islamic holiday month of Ramadan is observed in Azerbaijan. Respect religious and cultural customs and laws at this time. During Ramadan, if you're not fasting, don’t eat, drink or smoke around people who are. Seek local advice so you don’t offend. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan. Azerbaijan's official tourism board describes the country as secular, with no enforced religious dress code in public; Western clothing is normal, especially in Baku.
